newsitem.title: USA: No U.S.-EU meat agreement yet - EU official.
newsitem.headline: No U.S.-EU meat agreement yet - EU official.

text.p: U.S. and EU officials have been unable to settle a dispute over meat imports, the senior EU negotiator at the talks said Thursday, and EU negotiators were headed back to Brussels later in the day.

"The talks have been somewhat disappointing," said Lars Hoelgaard, the EU leader. Hoelgaard said the two sides would continue to communicate and the EU has invited U.S. officials to continue the talks in Brussels next week.

Hoelgaard told reporters that there had been some progress in poultry issues during talks Thursday morning. The key sticking point of the talks has been the U.S. poultry industry's use of chlorine as a decontaminant.
"The question of decontamination has become less acute," Hoelgaard said.
The EU previously proposed a scientific review of decontamination methods using lactic acid and TSP, trisodium phosphate, but not chlorine.
Asked if the EU would allow chlorine to be studied as well, Hoelgaard said, "we should leave this issue to the scientists."
Hoelgaard said there were still issues to be resolved as regards to regionalization and how the United States officially recognizes the animal health status in the European Union.

The failure to reach an agreement in the so-called veterinary equivalency talks has already halted U.S. poultry shipments to Europe and could halt European meat products to the United States on April 30.
Washington has threatened to remove more than 100 European meat and poultry plants from its list of approved exporters on April 30 if there is no agreement.
Hoelgaard repeated warnings that such action by Washington would harm the situation and would "trigger appropriate action on our side."
U.S. officials were not immediately available to discuss the talks or developments in the dispute.
